data.review_body:
As has happened before, the customer has to pay for an item that doesn’t work! But the real problem lies in the way the customer HAS to provide evidence. It’s not always possible to provide a ridiculous photo or an equally ridiculous – and, above all, pointless – video to prove that the device doesn’t work!! 
And ‘obviously’, the customer who makes a complaint in good faith also HAS to bear the cost of a faulty device. 
In short, in my case, I’ve been ‘robbed’ of a handful of dollars, but I’ll carry on living happily ever after 💚, whilst the manufacturer of the camera 👎 that doesn’t work will, as far as I’m concerned, always remain a fraudster.
Furthermore, Aliexpress’s dispute resolution policy needs to be more concrete and realistic when it comes to evidence!

data.review_body: Aliexpres has become a haven for fraud and fakes. I noticed a seller a 12 piece spanner set for sale at a ridiculously cheap price (A good sign of a scam). When I looked closer at the listing even though all of the photos and the description were of a spanner set there was a single photo of what they were actually selling. It was a cheap set of allen keys. 5 people had already left 1 star reviews as they had been conned. I reported the listing to AE to try and stop other people losing money. Aliexpress decision was that the seller was doing nothing wrong and allowed the scam to continue. While AE actively support this type of fraudulent listing it is a very unsafe place to buy from.
data.review_headline: Aliexpres has become a haven for fraud…
